analyticalQuestion: Which part of the full Fourier--Leray equation admits a scale-critical scalar upper bound, which frequency class saturates it, and can the existing nontrivial scalar charge be extended to arbitrary data without selecting a frame?
supportedClaim: The full Fourier--Leray term has a finite scale-critical heat-Duhamel bound in E_nu; the exact high--high-to-low family has normalized critical symbol ratio one for every positive integer N despite unbounded input/output separation; and every convolution-additive, rotation-invariant scalar charge is zero.

chartContract.takeaway: Critical scalar degree control is finite, but high--high-to-low interactions remove any gain from scale separation and a nontrivial additive scalar charge cannot also be rotation invariant.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: The all-frequency scaling, bilinear, saturation, and charge no-go statements are analytic theorems. The plotted rows and the 200,000-triad, 15,624-rotation, degree-256 Catalan audit are exact deterministic regressions, not substitutes for the proofs.
